pr_title: Use Roslyn interceptors feature in binder gen
pr_comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-extensions-configuration See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/89322. **Work left** - [ ] Add suppression logic for linker warnings - [ ] Fix name clash issue between assemblies (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/86363) - [ ] Mop up an extra generation in baselines (e.g. `AsConfigWithChildren` when there are no collection/object members)
Author: layomia
Assignees: layomia
Labels: `area-Extensions-Configuration`
Milestone: 8.0.0
🎉 🎉 🎉 Reviewers - let's have a look at this and try to get feedback in and addressed ASAP to make it for RC1.
Can repro CI failures locally, working through them.

### Closing notes

**Name clashes**

Not needed for this feature to work & there's no new risk added here. I'll address in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/86363. I've reverted the changes to the options generator and left out unique name generation in this generator.

**Testing**

There's always room to improve coverage, but I believe these suffice for merging this PR.

- Interceptors handling multiple calls, including across different files.
  - [Emitted source](https://gist.github.com/layomia/2746af1b0ca0da385ac9bec2fe55cc6b) for the binder test project shows this is well covered.
- Diagnostic suppressions where applicable
  - numerous binding calls in extensions assemblies which are linker trimmed show that this handled correctly
- Not suppressing diagnostics for calls we didn't intercept:
  - tested with simple console application
-  Polymorphic type handling: Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Console assembly exercises/validates the updated logic.
Test failures seem to be caused by applying the code analysis version update across all projects. Will fix.

Can take this opportunity to fix https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/86363.

@tarekgh @ericstj @eiriktsarpalis looks like the interceptors feature [requires `<Features>$(Features);InterceptorsPreview</Features>`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/48817/files#r1256032359) in consuming projects. ~~While the feature is in preview,~~ it seems we should update the SDK to set it if `EnableConfigurationBindingGenerator` is set. Otherwise users would need to set two properties to use the generator.

The Web SDK already sets the feature property when binding & RDG generates are enabled, so the concern is about regular SDK scenarios.
@layomia does the interceptor feature will be released the same way? I mean users have to opt-in to get it. Or is this temporary for preview and will change when it gets released?
Yes I believe interceptors will be shipped as a preview feature in GA. cc @captainsafia.

We can do the same thing as RDG here.  Just add us to this condition:
https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/b3b5a2800d4de997572068332bf222e2e8f808d5/src/WebSdk/ProjectSystem/Targets/Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web.ProjectSystem.targets#L62-L65

We could do the same in our nuget package targets:
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Binder/src/buildTransitive/Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.Binder.targets

Might be good to have a safeguard in the generator just in case someone manages to invoke it without setting that property.  I suspect RDG needs the same as well (eg Web class library that get's referenced by a normal app or class library).

review_comments:
>LanguageVersion [](http://example.com/codeflow?start=20&length=15)

I assume we have a code checks language version to be at least 11 and produce diagnostics if it is not. If so, do we have a test for this?
never mind, I see the test in other file now.

Did we want to add something like https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/4249701de6f005c670c7f371141e772d02f89156/src/WebSdk/ProjectSystem/Targets/Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web.ProjectSystem.targets#L64 to our NuGet package targets, or will we ask users to set this?  @eerhardt @tarekgh @captainsafia
I think we decided to mimic whatever the aspnet is doing in the web project.
ASP.NET doesn't ship a nuget package so we're special here.  There's an ongoing discussion around this to decide what we want to do.
Is there a possibility that a configuration binder method call exists in the compilation that hasn't been intercepted by the source generator, and if so, could this create an invalid suppression?
Do we have unit tests checking that the suppressor doesn't end up suppressing other RUC/RDC warnings in the compilation that are unrelated to the configuration binder?

@layomia I can show you the setup that I used for the RDG to validate the behavior of the suppressor.

Unfortunately, I wasn't able to merge it to main since it doesn't play nice in Helix environments (it requires loading the linker analyzer assembly) but it can help to smoke test.

nit: could you please add a comment with the following info?
```
IL2026: Members attributed with RequiresUnreferencedCode may break when trimming
IL3050: Avoid calling members annotated with 'RequiresDynamicCodeAttribute' when publishing as native AOT
```

We don't need to generate typed interceptors for each `ConfigurationBinder.Bind` invocation anymore. Strong typing facilitated the generated methods being preferred by the compiler over the framework's.

Instead, we generate one interceptor for each overload that's called and funnel into one `BindCoreMain` method with type checks. This simplifies the generator's input parsing logic and reduces the size of emitted code (though not by a lot for typical usage which should only have a few binding invocations/target config types).

Input objects will now be boxed. However, given the overall implementation (can provide details), any perf impact with the added type checks will only affect direct calls to `Bind` (not the primary/common use case). Wrt. boxing, only reference types are valid inputs to the methods.
This is worth adding it as a comment in the code. It is really helpful.

Will do... 

However, we might need to bring back strong typing to handle polymorphism, I'll circle back.

---

Update: ended up needing to generate an interceptor for each bind call, so the comment no longer applies.
